results.reader_title: European tile producers respond differently to supply shocks
results.reader_what: A simulation finds stronger pricing power can cushion input shocks while more competitive firms adjust sourcing faster.
results.reader_why: Different industrial market positions imply different forms of supply-chain resilience under international input disruptions.

Higher-value market positions produce greater robustness to input-cost pressure; firms under stronger competition adapt procurement more readily. The results are theoretical simulations, not direct observations of actual post-war sourcing changes. The text is an accepted journal pre-proof.

admission.reason: Directly measures the European versus US AI growth-financing gap, which bears on European control and scaling of critical technology.

results.reader_title: Europe’s AI startups face a scale-up funding gap
results.reader_what: Europe matches US AI funding-round counts more closely than investment volume, indicating weaker scale-up financing.
results.reader_why: Less growth capital can constrain European firms’ ability to scale strategically important AI technologies.
results.reader_more: Using approximately 8,000 AI venture-capital rounds from 2000–2025, the authors compare Europe and the US around the 2021 generative-AI inflection. Europe approaches the US in deal counts but AI captured about 31% of European venture-capital investment versus around 60% in the US after 2021. Difference-in-differences and sensitivity tests support a funding-intensity gap, not proof of one institutional cause.

deep_analysis.research_question: Has European AI venture financing scaled differently from US financing since 2021?
deep_analysis.main_finding: Europe has similar AI deal activity but a much smaller capital share and funding volume than the US, particularly after 2021.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Roughly 8,000 PitchBook AI venture rounds, World Bank covariates, difference-in-differences, event studies, placebo tests and alternative sample exclusions.
deep_analysis.qualification: Observational differences and timing-based estimates do not prove that a particular financial institution caused the gap; Europe includes the UK in main estimates.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Direct Strand A route 2 evidence of an AI industrial-capital capability gap relevant to European technological sovereignty.
